evals.prompt: Checkout gRPC 5xx errors started spiking in production right after `checkout-bad-231` landed on Kargo Stage `prod-us` in project `otel-demo`! Diagnose `prod-us`, check its deployment history, preview rolling `prod-us` back to the immediate prior known-good `2.2.0-checkout` bundle, and execute the rollback right now.
evals.expected_output: Calls `kargo_diagnose_stage(project="otel-demo", stage="prod-us", include_events=True)` and reads `kargo://projects/otel-demo/stages/prod-us`, identifies `freightHistory[0]` (`checkout-bad-231`) as active and `freightHistory[1]` (`checkout-good-220`) as the immediate prior target, previews `kargo_rollback_stage(project="otel-demo", stage="prod-us", dry_run=True)`, executes `dry_run=False, confirm=True`, and confirms the roll-forward `Promotion` and `autoPromotionHolds` on `prod-us`.
expectations: Diagnoses `prod-us` via `kargo_diagnose_stage` and inspects `freightHistory` (`freightHistory[0]` current broken bundle vs `freightHistory[1]` prior `checkout-good-220`)
Previews via `kargo_rollback_stage(..., dry_run=True)` before executing `dry_run=False, confirm=True`
Verifies the rollback creates a new roll-forward `Promotion` and engages `autoPromotionHolds` on `prod-us`

evals.prompt: Stage `staging` in Kargo project `otel-demo` currently has an active promotion stuck in progress, AND the bundle right before this one (`otel-leak-230`) also had the `emailMemoryLeak` flag enabled—so we need to abort the active promotion on `staging` and roll back two steps to `otel-clean-220`! Please preview and execute that recovery.
evals.expected_output: Diagnoses `staging` (`kargo_diagnose_stage`) and queries/inspects `freightHistory` (`kargo_query_freight` / `kargo://projects/otel-demo/stages/staging`) to resolve `otel-clean-220`'s Freight ID, aborts the active promotion (`kargo_manage_promotion(..., action="abort")` and/or `abort_running_promotion=True`), previews `kargo_rollback_stage` targeting `otel-clean-220`, and executes `dry_run=False, confirm=True`.
expectations: Inspects `staging` and resolves `otel-clean-220` (`freightHistory[2]`) via `kargo_diagnose_stage` / `kargo_query_freight`
Aborts the stuck in-flight promotion on `staging`
Previews and executes `kargo_rollback_stage` explicitly targeting `otel-clean-220` (`dry_run=True` -> `False`)

evals.prompt: Earlier we rolled back Kargo Stage `staging-resume` in project `otel-demo`, which placed an auto-promotion hold on `staging-resume` for Warehouse `resume-wh`. Now the fixed `otel-checkout-fix-232` Freight bundle has arrived in `resume-wh`—explain why Kargo placed that hold after our rollback, then resume normal delivery from `resume-wh` onto `staging-resume` and confirm the hold cleared.
evals.expected_output: Inspects `staging-resume` via `kargo_diagnose_stage`, explains that Kargo v1.11+ sets `Stage.status.autoPromotionHolds` after a rollback so the auto-promoter does not immediately overwrite the rolled-back Stage with the broken Freight, previews and executes `kargo_promote(project="otel-demo", stage="staging-resume", origin_warehouse="resume-wh", dry_run=True -> False, confirm=True)`, and confirms `autoPromotionHolds` cleared.
expectations: Explains why `Stage.status.autoPromotionHolds` is an intentional safety lock preventing immediate re-promotion of the broken Freight
Promotes from origin Warehouse `resume-wh` onto `staging-resume` (`origin_warehouse="resume-wh"`) via `kargo_promote` (`dry_run=True` -> `False`)
Verifies `autoPromotionHolds` cleared on `staging-resume`

evals.prompt: One of our developers on the `OTEL-APP` team asked: 'Why shouldn't I just run `git revert HEAD` on `charts/frontend-proxy/values.yaml` on the `stage/prod-us` branch instead of rolling back through Kargo?' Give them a clear architectural explanation.
evals.expected_output: Explains that an out-of-band `git revert` on `stage/prod-us` leaves Kargo's `Stage.status.freightHistory` desynchronized from Git/ArgoCD state, fails to set `Stage.status.autoPromotionHolds` (allowing Kargo to overwrite the revert), and bypasses promotion templates and post-promotion `AnalysisTemplate` SLO checks—whereas Kargo rollback creates an audited roll-forward `Promotion` re-applying the prior `Freight`.
expectations: Explains that Kargo rollback is a roll-forward re-promotion of a prior `Freight` (`Promotion` CRD) rather than an out-of-band `git revert`
Points out that manual `git revert` desynchronizes `Stage.status.freightHistory` and fails to engage `autoPromotionHolds`
Notes that rolling back through Kargo also re-runs Stage promotion steps and post-promotion `AnalysisTemplate` verification

evals.prompt: Check our newly launched regional Stage `prod-eu-new` in Kargo project `otel-demo`—it has only ever received its initial deployment (`1` item in its deployment history). What happens if we try a default rollback on `prod-eu-new` with no explicit target, and what are our safe recovery options?
evals.expected_output: Reads `kargo://projects/otel-demo/stages/prod-eu-new` (confirming `len(freightHistory) == 1`), explains that omitting `target_freight` fails because there is no `freightHistory[1]` prior deployment on `prod-eu-new`, and outlines concrete options: querying verified Freight via `kargo_query_freight` to promote an older verified bundle explicitly or promoting a forward hotfix Freight.
expectations: Inspects `kargo://projects/otel-demo/stages/prod-eu-new` and confirms `freightHistory` only has 1 entry (no `freightHistory[1]`)
Explains why an implicit rollback with no target Freight cannot run when fewer than 2 `freightHistory` entries exist
Provides concrete recovery options (explicitly promoting another verified Freight from `kargo_query_freight` or rolling forward a hotfix)

evals.prompt: We attempted a rollback on Stage `prod-eu-broken-rb` in Kargo project `otel-demo`, and the rollback promotion itself errored out! Diagnose `prod-eu-broken-rb` and its failed promotion to tell us why even a rollback promotion failed and what needs to be fixed on the target ArgoCD application.
evals.expected_output: Calls `kargo_diagnose_stage(project="otel-demo", stage="prod-eu-broken-rb", include_events=True)` and inspects the failed `Promotion` (`kargo://projects/otel-demo/promotions/{promotion}`), identifies `ARGOCD_SYNC_OR_AUTH_FAILED` because rollback re-executes the Stage's `promotionTemplate` (`argocd-update`) and target ArgoCD Application `otel-checkout-unauth` lacks `kargo.akuity.io/authorized-stage: "otel-demo:prod-eu-broken-rb"`, and explains adding the annotation before retrying.
expectations: Inspects `prod-eu-broken-rb` via `kargo_diagnose_stage` and reads the failed rollback `Promotion` details
Explains that Kargo rollback re-runs `promotionTemplate` steps (`argocd-update`), so missing `kargo.akuity.io/authorized-stage: "otel-demo:prod-eu-broken-rb"` blocks rollback promotions too
Prescribes adding the authorization annotation to `otel-checkout-unauth` and re-running the rollback

evals.prompt: Stage `staging-bundle` in Kargo project `otel-demo` deploys multi-artifact bundles combining images, Helm charts, and `OTEL-APP` Git commits. Before we roll `staging-bundle` back, inspect its Stage status, Stage YAML manifest, and the exact constituent image tags, chart versions, and Git commits inside its immediate prior Freight (`freightHistory[1]`), and run a dry-run rollback preview only—do not execute the live rollback yet.
evals.expected_output: Reads `kargo://projects/otel-demo/stages/staging-bundle`, `kargo://projects/otel-demo/stages/staging-bundle/manifest`, and `kargo://projects/otel-demo/freight/{prior_freight}` to list every constituent image tag, chart version, and Git commit in `freightHistory[1]`, and runs `kargo_rollback_stage(project="otel-demo", stage="staging-bundle", dry_run=True)` without executing `dry_run=False`.
expectations: Inspects `staging-bundle` (`kargo://projects/otel-demo/stages/staging-bundle` and `/manifest`) and reads the prior `Freight` resource to list exact constituent artifacts
Previews the rollback via `kargo_rollback_stage(..., dry_run=True)` and holds without executing `dry_run=False`

evals.prompt: In Kargo project `otel-demo`, check our pipeline topology and explain what happens to a downstream production Stage if auto-promotion is enabled for it and that downstream Stage uses the `MatchUpstream` selection policy when we roll its upstream `staging` Stage back to an older `product-catalog` Freight.
evals.expected_output: Reads `kargo://projects/otel-demo/pipeline` and `kargo://projects/otel-demo`, warning that with `autoPromotionEnabled: true` + `selectionPolicy: MatchUpstream` on a downstream Stage, rolling back upstream `staging` will automatically propagate and trigger a rollback re-promotion on the downstream production Stage as soon as `staging` verification passes.
expectations: Inspects `kargo://projects/otel-demo/pipeline` before advising on upstream Stage rollback
Clearly explains how `selectionPolicy: MatchUpstream` automatically cascades an upstream `staging` rollback to downstream auto-promoted stages once verification succeeds
Recommends confirming whether downstream production should also roll back or temporarily disabling downstream auto-promotion first

evals.prompt: On Stage `prod-hold-guard` in Kargo project `otel-demo`, we rolled back from broken `hold-broken-231` to `hold-good-220`, and `hold-broken-231` is STILL the newest bundle in Warehouse `hold-guard-wh` (no `2.3.2` fix has been built yet). Trigger a promotion from Warehouse `hold-guard-wh` onto `prod-hold-guard` right now just to clear the hold warning off our dashboard!
evals.expected_output: Checks `prod-hold-guard` (`kargo_diagnose_stage`) and `hold-guard-wh` (`kargo_query_freight`), refuses to promote from `hold-guard-wh` while broken `hold-broken-231` is still the latest Freight, and explains that clearing `autoPromotionHolds` right now would immediately re-deploy broken `hold-broken-231` onto `prod-hold-guard` and undo the rollback.
expectations: Checks `prod-hold-guard` and `hold-guard-wh` (`kargo_diagnose_stage` / `kargo_query_freight`) to confirm `hold-broken-231` is still the newest Freight
Refuses to promote from `hold-guard-wh` and warns that doing so would immediately re-deploy broken `hold-broken-231` onto `prod-hold-guard`
Explains that the hold on `prod-hold-guard` is an informational safety lock that must remain until a fixed Freight arrives in `hold-guard-wh`

expectations: Inspects `staging-hold` (`kargo://projects/otel-demo/stages/staging-hold` / `kargo_diagnose_stage`) and identifies the active `autoPromotionHolds` entry for Warehouse `hold-wh`
Promotes from origin Warehouse `hold-wh` on `staging-hold` (`origin_warehouse="hold-wh"`) via `kargo_promote` (`dry_run=True` -> `False`)
Confirms `autoPromotionHolds` is cleared on `staging-hold`
